full_text: I REJECT A WORLD THIS PAINFULLY STUPID, AND YOU SHOULD TOO Hi! How’s everyone? Sorry I haven’t been writing much lately. I’ve been sick. From the light. Some summers are like that. Vampire blues. And maybe the truth is also… I don’t know what to say. LOL. That’s rare for me. But I suppose the world has changed. And so have I. I feel like estranged from the times we’re in. They’re alien to me. I watch people around me. And I wonder. Why do they want to waste their lives like this ? On this? I’m sure you know what I mean. The narcotic haze of the screen. Me, me, me. Nothing, nothing, nothing. Van Gogh once said: “art is to console those who are broken by life.” What did he mean by that? Why does it matter? What’s my point? Where am I going with all this? Shit, Umair, where’s the hook! You need to reel them in in the first ten letters! Fuck Van Gogh! Show Me The Money! I don’t know what to say about the world now. Wait, that’s wrong. I don’t think there is anything worth saying about it, except exactly that. What can you say about…nothing? I look at the times, the world, and now? I feel nothing, anymore, about it. I shrug. I have better things to do with my time, consciousness, energy, than waste it on this . It isn’t appropriate, or healthy, to care about people who don’t care about themselves. What’s the point of a broken heart? That question goes deeper than you might think. Van Gogh wondered, too. He looked at fields, trees, skies, and saw them in a new way. What do you see when you look at the world? Here’s what I do. What can you say about…the kind of shocking stupidity…absolute cowardice…all-consuming idiocy…we’re surrounded in, by? I’m sure that there are people who can talk about it endlessly. Someone call Ezra Klein or Mehdi Hasan or who have you. It’s a long list, mostly men, and they all have this constant look of outrage slash bewilderment. Wow, as if it’s all such a puzzle. Such good boys. Me? I wonder: why bother? Are these guys serious? LOL. Don’t they see the world we live in now? Let me say the quiet part out loud. People have made their choices. And they’re fucking idiotic ones. Should the rest of us, the thoughtful, sensible, and kind ones, go on wasting our lives on these hopeless, pathetic idiots? Trying to save them…from themselves? That’s what we’ve been taught to do. But it’s wrong. And this is the genuinely great moral and intellectual question before us. Not: can we save the world, fix democracy, end war, hunger, etcetera. LOL. We failed at that . That part’s over. Because people are just incomprehensibly stupid, and getting stupider by the microsecond . Now it’s: how much more of us do we waste on people who’ve liquified their brains into gray neural mush, who genuinely like existing in a completely mindless way, whose hollowed out cortexes only contain tiny needles endlessly automatically dispensing dopamine hits of TikTok, YouTube, demagogues, hate, rage, conspiracies, influencers, AI girlfriends, or whatever dumb fuck shit it is this day, month, year? Have you ever seen a human mind implode into slurry? You’re living in it. Those of us who have, I don’t know, three functioning brain cells left know how these choices end . Know, not guess, suppose, imagine, or speculate. Guess what, we read a book or two. And yet. There’s the “surprised” Trumpist in that corner, wondering why they’re getting poorer, there’s the angry man-child in that one, whining about how girls don’t like him, as if being a sullen, sulking, misogynist was The World’s Most Powerful Aphrodisiac, LOL, there’s some poor guy over there, blaming an ocean-borne baby with the wrong skin color for his own failed life, instead of examining his painfully stupid adoration of the very monsters who exploit him. Maybe you want to waste your life on this. Not me. Not anymore. We’re living in their fantasy. Where do we draw the line and back away? You know what I have to say about that? Fuck it. I exit. I reject it. Je refuse. I am out, finished, done trying to save these pathetic morons. You live in this tawdry, worthless fantasy, dumb fuck. But don’t ask me to, not anymore, and don’t fucking count on people like me to save you from your own stupidity anymore, either. We shouldn’t. I prefer a life . Consciousness, truth, beauty, joy, love. I want to live . You die this death by a thousand billionaires, demagogues, stupidities, self-destructions. I am going to live . You’ve chosen death, which is what all this is, in lethally real ways, by the way. Hence, absolutely, with total certainty, fuck the destiny of slavery, self-destruction and stupidity — and then claiming perpetual victimhood over it, and then coming crying to people like us to save you once you see the mess you’ve made, oh no, I want democracy back, I want a future, I want money, don’t let them take it all from me — you’ve chosen. Fuck that loop of ruin. So… What is there left to say now? Nothing. Let AI babble over what’s left of us. We’re already dead inside. Something in us broke over the last decade or so. Everything in us did. Minds, spirits, souls, intellect, moral horizon, imagination, sociality, decency, the idea that we’re to be anything but obedient little narcissists bowing and scraping before the very systems which diminish and enslave us. What a fate that is. To become something like a willing slave, an accomplice to your self-destruction, to press the button on your own dehumanization. But people do this every day now, cheering, smiling, giggling, laughing. They don’t know anything else. And let’s face it: as much as we’ve tried, we can’t teach them a damned thing. Why is that? LOL, who cares . Maybe it’s wrong of me to say that. But for the first time in my life, I myself don’t want to face the answer. We all know the answer, by the way. People are really this weak. They’re really this stupid. It’s surreal, but everything we’ve accomplished in human civilization over millennia, from Aristotle and Plato’s first schools to universities to science to literature to art — none of it in the end has been able to teach these idiots a thing. Not one thing. Not…one. I mean that. Not…democracy’s good for you, dummy. Not…the system that exploits you is never going to free you, so try to oppose it. Not…immense concentrations of wealth and power are bad for societies. Not…everyone deserves dignity and resources and respect. Not…there are inviolable rights which are the foundation of the project of civilization, and that project is about fulfilling one’s self, not in narcissistic way, but in an expansive, noble, lasting one. Fuck, not one of these lessons has sunk in. It’s not just dispiriting when you think about it, it’s also amazing, because before us we appear to be witnessing the death of the human spirit, in all its forms. What can you say to people who appear to be dead inside in every way? Are they listening? Should you bother? Hey, you scream, listen, you’re…slitting your own fucking throat! That’s not a necklace, it’s a razor blade. But who gets hurt when you try to take a weapon away from a suicidal lunatic? You. We can. Analyze it, psychoanalyze it, dissect it, justify it, rationalize it, explain it, intellectualize it. We can proffer each other, thoughtful people that we are, every kind of rationale under the sun, from economics to childhood trauma to social isolation to emotional and material deprivation to historical cycles to biochemistry and on and on and on. And you know what? That doesn’t matter anymore, either. Because these aren’t children we’re talking about, and more to the point, it’s not them that we need to focus on anymore. Oh no, these poor babies, won’t someone cry for them, they’re the world’s real victims. not little children dying when bombs rip them apart. Sorry, I can’t think of people like that anymore. Now I see these fucking morons as accomplices in, to, their own undoing. And I have little to no sympathy for them anymore, because it’s not my place to. Their own self-destruction is both the crime and the punishment. And no, I can’t “respect” that “choice,” as fashionable as it is to parrot therapy-speak and pretend we must respect everyone’s choices for everything. Some choices really are fatally fucking stupid. So there’s nothing — zero — left to talk about if you ask me. At least in the way we’re used to speaking about it. How did the world end up here? For fuck’s sake , we all know by now. Can we just cut the bullshit? Can we stop fucking pretending? Look at these idiots . Do you think they’re even capable of forming a complete adult sentence at this point, let alone nurturing democracy or civilization? Where’s the world going next? Kill me with a pleasant, warm cyanide bath, fucking rip my eyes out, Oedipus…Jesus…for the love of… for fuck’s sake , we all know . Just… look at these idiots . These are people who can gush over 25 TikTok influencers, but probably can’t name 25, I don’t know, great minds in history, artists, poets, scientists, heads of state, anybody. Do you think they’re capable of understanding or admitting the gravity of the mistakes they’ve made? I don’t. So are things going to change? For fuck’s…sake. We all know that one, too. Look at these fucking idiots. The more we try to teach them, the less they learn. You know what that makes us? The real fucking idiots. We were taught: no, no, you have to waste your life trying to save the idiots. With art, science, literature, truth, beauty, goodness, knowledge, reason. Fuck that! Fuck it to bits. It was wrong . Nothing could have been more wrong, in fact. I for one am not going to be the greater idiot anymore. If these fools want to destroy themselves, hey, by all means, go for it. I’m not going to get in the way anymore. I’m not going to waste another moment of my life trying to stop it all. I’m sorry I wasted so much of it already. My mistake. I wish I’d been more of a cynical, evil, ruthless bastard, because, fuck, look at us decent and thoughtful people, where we’ve all ended up. We’re the ones who got fucked. Admit it, if you have the balls. I know you probably don’t, but this is the only place real change begins for any of us or all of us. Tell me you don’t feel like you wasted your life, too. Go ahead, lie to me. And for that reason, I now celebrate the dummies fucking themselves over for a change. Let them, cheer them on, applaud them, don’t, don’t try to fucking stop them anymore. It’s the least they deserve. I have nothing left to say about it all for that very reason. I failed, we failed, all our paradigms failed, and everything we wanted for the world was a stupid joke. That sounds bitter, but it’s not. It’s a relief. Let’s face the fucking truth. Let’s say the quiet part out loud. Let’s not overthink it anymore. “The average person” is a total moron . And that’s being kind. Someone basically incapable of understanding, wanting, needing, aspiring to anything more than fuck, eat, kill. That is why they’re so easily seduced, by things as mind-blowingly idiotic as fucking endless scroll algorithms drip-feeding them cheap fantasies of sex-violence-money-power, an infinite loop of pure death drive, and it’s why all the lessons of the last ten millennia have come to nothing, yet again. What’s the point of a…broken heart? I don’t have anything left to say. Except on that subject. I was wrong. The bad guys were right . People aren’t worth what we offered them, all these beautiful treasures, civilization, democracy, science, art, literature. Not in my eyes, just objectively speaking. Look at the state of things, LOL. Who did all that? “The average person” did, whoever the fuck that is, which is everybody, nobody, somebody, anybody. Let it all burn. Pour fuel on the flames. Isn’t it all in flames, anyways? What’s the point of a broken heart? Who gives a fuck about an age this pathetic, stupid, futile, so much so that even calling it tragic assigns it a nobility it doesn’t have? Who should? I don’t anymore. Neither should you. Our responsibility ends here. The bad guys were right. That’s not tragic, and it’s not noble. There’s no art or beauty or even truth in that. There’s just a sense of emptiness. Bad guys are dumb. Smart people tend to be good. And so the tragedy, my friends, is people like us. We have no place in this world now. We are looking for a thing that doesn’t exist. The bad guys were right about the bottomless stupidity of “the average person,” and they were right too, about us, about the futility and even deeper stupidity of trying to be good, decent, and wise, if and when people are only raw appetites of fuck-eat-kill. What is there left to say after that? What’s the point of science, literature, art, etcetera, after that? LOL, is there one? Fuck it, let AI have it, and let the fascists have the rest. Enjoy that future, motherfuckers. I hope you like being poor and enslaved. If these mighty pillars of civilization all crumble in the grim teeth of the endless loop of “save the fucking idiots from themselves,” then I for one am finished with that eternal recurrence. Fuck that, you be the one to try and save the fucking idiots from themselves. Good luck wasting your life on that particular endeavor. The point of a broken heart is to find someone else with one, too. And in that people like us are different . We’re not just looking for broken reflections of ourselves in algorithms, mirrors, likes, fans, followers, we’re not just raw zombie appetites screaming fuck-eat-kill-fuck-eat-kill. We’re not just one endless narcissism imploding into nothing. The edges of a broken heart only fit around, into, with another one. And this is the point of it all, civilization, art, science, literature, life, all of it. Love. Does anyone fucking remember that? They don’t, because people are really this fucking stupid . So much so that they’ve done this to the world. All of this, and I don’t have to recite the facts for you. And yet here we are, watching a world incapable of even trying to lift a finger to live up to this most ancient, simple, and obvious of truths. So fuck, and I really mean it, fuck to the very last fuck-eat-kill at the final edge of sweet oblivion all of the dumb fuck spiritually bankrupt and intellectually decrepit morons who’ve done this to us, the world, the future, themselves. They’re not worth a second of any of it anymore, my life, yours, civilization, all of it, tout. C’est finis. I’ll be at the cafe, with the ghosts of all the broken hearted. Van Gogh’s whispering. Can you hear him? They’re the only people I talk to anymore. Love, Umair (and Snowy!) http://www.umairhaque.org PS — — → BONUS SNOWY AND UMAIR PIC!!!!!!!!!!!! title: You Cannot Analyze Your Way Into Feeling Alive
label: human
full_text: Vitality does not care about your vernacular Photo by Mr. Great Heart Many people, when they think they are talking about their feelings, are actually doing one of the following instead: Ruminating on an external story or circumstance of what he, she, or they did, how much of a “narcissist” they were, or all they did wrong Intellectualizing, labeling, and categorizing by way of learned terminology and frameworks Neither of these are feelings. And neither of them will ever in a million years (or countless cycles) ever yield a state of feeling truly alive. On the contrary, they are stifling, limiting, and flat, devoid of a real internal experience. Feeling alive requires internal experiencing In other words: feelings. This is not to say you have to move through life being “overly-sensitive,” or “soppy,” or subject to taking everything personally, or coming undone at the wrong time and place. But it does mean that if you’d like to move through life with a general sense of vitality and aliveness and connection to it, that relational strength really has to begin in you. If we want to feel alive, we have to also feel things inside. Feelings aren’t found in “frameworks” Your feelings don’t care about the labels. Some parts of you may, and it may seem soothing to your conscious and cognitive anxiety, seeking to strike a sense of security by lining up plastic walls in a tote in which to toss things, but these actually do nothing for your underlying lived experience or longterm sense of vitality. It’s why doing this can feel soothing in the moment, but you still feel so drained, beaten down, hardened, or worn out in the long run. Feelings don’t need frameworks. They just need contact. When things come up, we look at them rather than dismissing them or handing them to someone else, or doing something externally, to equally “make them go away.” When we experience things, go or bad, really let that awareness register and move through its cycle and release on its own. And if we do this with everything (or most things) throughout our day, we will over time build a weave of fabric that is permeable but also strong. It can provide a beautiful net in which to support ourselves as we move through life, and also catch things we would’ve otherwise let slip by, that serve our sense of being a part of it, i.e., aliveness.

title: You Will Never Feel The Highs Unless You Feel The Lows
label: human
full_text: Ebbs require flow Photo by Austin Neill A lot of people move through life unable to feel much of anything meaningful. Often, they may not even feel “lows” other than the occasional melancholy (and very often, they may not even feel that.) Rather, many of us move through life as though surrounded by a constant “white,” or enveloped in a cloud of “gray,” and we may know we don’t feel “everyday emotion,” even if we don’t realize that not everyone lives like this. We may feel that we have to chase things down and turn up the volume to even hear anything; that, in the words of Goo Goo Dolls in their 1998 hit Iris: “yeah, you bleed just to know you’re alive.” Or, in the words of Nicolas Cage’s character from the 2018 film Spider-Verse: “sometimes I let matches burn down to my fingertips just to feel something, anything.” And we don’t usually mean this literally, or physically, but rather to say: it takes a lot to feel anything. I was one of these people. For most of my adult life I lived a way that I knew was pretty “even keel,” but didn’t recognize as being particularly notable until I psychologist with a PhD asked me, “what’s the most common emotion you feel everyday?” The question was so bizarre to me that he might as well have been asking “what color balloon do you typically carry?” Like, I understood the concept, and had certainly held a balloon before, but the very idea of doing so not only every day, but in multiple ways, with multiple different colors, was mind-blowing (and frankly, life changing.) The reason many of us don’t actually feel “the highs” or “ups” is because we never let ourselves experience “the lows” or “downs.” If you suppress one end of a wavelength, it’s going to dampen the other side, too. If you arrest the movement of a swing at one end, it’s going to fall flat before it reaches the full arc on the other side. Suppressing emotions to avoid pain creates emotional flatness. Research shows that constant emotional suppression dampens the experience of positive feelings, leading to numbness and chronic stress rather than the intended control. Discomfort with “unpleasant” emotions creates a shortcoming with “pleasant” emotions. If we withhold our full human experience in some areas, it seeps into our ability to fully The solution to wanting to feel more joy and happiness is not in forcing happiness, but rather allowing ourselves to fully experience our human capacity, which includes feeling sadness, anger, fear, etc. Because the human expression does not intuitively understand our arbitrary assessment of what’s “good” vs. “bad,” even if this judgment is submerged within our own subconscious. When we suppress some emotion, the system learns over time to suppress all emotion. To feel happy, genuinely, we have to lean into the full kaleidoscope of human feelings, starting with everything we feel day to day, however tiny. The solution is in acknowledging and learning to become familiar with, and experience, the myriad of things that course through us every day, big or small.

title: High Contrast Winter
label: human
full_text: The Alchemy of a Shared Bookshelf I took three books with me when I left home for college. Space was limited in a dorm room; besides, I wanted to travel light. So I selected the best of the best from my personal library. I could have included The Catcher in the Rye, but that would have been obvious, pretentious, and ultimately impossible, since I didn’t own a copy. My personal library was not a collection of books I was assigned to read in high school. It was a collection of books and comics I actually wanted to read. My personal best of the best: No One Gets Out of Here Alive , by Jerry Hopkins. This is a biography of Jim Morrison, the lead singer of The Doors. The book had a number of pictures of Morrison shirtless, just wearing low-cut, hip hugger, leather pants. Of course it made the list. Color Me Beautiful , by Carole Jackson. This was a wildly popular book from the early 1980s that helped women and their gay sons identify their most flattering colors based on their skin tone, hair color, and eye color by categorizing them into four seasonal color palettes: Winter, Spring, Summer, and Autumn. Each season has its own set of colors that are recommended for clothing, makeup, and accessories. My mother had our ‘colors done’ in the early eighties, and if you must know, I am a Low-contrast Winter, while my mother was a High-contrast Winter. That meant we could have easily shared clothes, were it not for the fact that my mother was 5’1”. Carrie , by Stephen King. Carrie is perfect. Period. My copy was so worn it had Scotch tape on the spine to keep it from falling apart and was heavily stained by Hawaiian Tropic suntan oil. Though it wasn’t in my library, I cannot continue without mentioning (in excruciating detail) the importance of the film version of Carrie . It is impossible to improve perfection. Like the word “unique,” it cannot be modified. Perfect is perfect. Period. The 1976 masterpiece Carrie , directed by Brian DePalma, is perfect. Period. Sissy Spacek, as the troubled teen who hits puberty, then decides to set her prom on fire, then flips a red Camaro cartwheel-style until it explodes, killing Nancy Allen and John Travolta, is perfect. Betty Buckley, as the gym teacher with a secret (wink), is perfect. Piper Laurie, as Carrie’s Jesus-obsessed mother with a crucifix kink, is beyond perfect (I broke my own rule). Her portrayal of Margaret White is a kind of perfect that transcends. It’s the kind of role that becomes part of your personality. Well, my personality. I quote one of her lines from the film at least once a day. It helps me remember there is good in a world that sometimes feels like a school gymnasium set ablaze. That felt really good. Thank you. This was my freshman dorm room personal library. No irony or humor; those were the books. I was delighted to discover that my freshman year roommate, Jonathan, brought the best of his personal library too, though he narrowed it down to one book only. The book, again without irony, was Ms. Piggy’s Guide to Life . I wasn’t familiar with the book, though the TV show The Muppets was a favorite of mine. The book gave the library depth, that is obvious. What neither of us knew was that the book would launch an unlikely lifelong friendship. This would surprise you if you were to witness how horrible our introduction was and how much we disliked each other for the first few weeks of school. Before we even met, he decided that I was an airhead from California because I played water polo and liked to lay in the sun (Jonathan had a very fair complexion). He nicknamed me “Thor”, which I mistakenly thought was a compliment. The stereotype and nickname were reinforced when, on orientation day, I went to lunch with Jonathan and his older sister Amy, along with her friend (I want to say) Lizbeth, or something similar. I had never met people like this. They wore black clothes and sported black sunglasses on a 90-degree day (with humidity, which was also completely new to me). They were beautiful, but in a different way than the sun-kissed kids I knew in California. Their skin, like Jonathan’s, suggested they spent most of their time inside, and they smoked a lot of cigarettes. Jonathan dressed in Brooks Brothers shirts, wing tip shoes; the kind of clothes my grandfather wore. But it was chic and very East Coast. I found it fascinating, though it wasn’t a look I could pull off. However, it was their distinctive way of speaking that mostly captured my attention. It was literally a foreign language, a hybrid English-French dialect spoken in such a way that the pitch of their voices rose at the end of each sentence (I later learned this was called “upspeak”). Even more astonishing was the subject they discussed most frequently: the social status and class of other people. The four of us wandered Thayer Street, the commercial drag that cut through the eastern edge of the campus, looking for a place to have lunch. We settled on a little café and got a table outside. Amy and Lizbeth had no interest in me whatsoever. Their attention was solely on Jonathan. They doted on him incessantly, speaking in baby-talk that veered on obscenity. Jonathan simply sat smiling, blushing bright red in contrast to his milky skin. This was turbocharged, fuel-injected cultural shock. Who are these people? Are they my age? Is everyone like this at Brown? I hadn’t met anyone else yet. My stomach dropped and I started to panic. What have I done? I don’t belong here. These are not my people. To make matters worse, oh so much worse, I mispronounced the name of the cheese Boursin, pronouncing it “Borsin.” “Oh great, they have Borsin,” I announced before ordering a pita filled with the creamy, flavorful cheese. Jonathan and his gang found this hilarious and proceeded to mock me for the rest of the meal by mentioning Borsin (pronouncing it as I had) as many times as possible in an attempt to humiliate me on my first day of college, in a place where I knew no one, 2500 miles away from home. It worked, of course. I was despondent. Jonathan and his sister Amy grew up in a small town in Southern New Jersey, not technically a part of France. Not once did the thought cross my mind to make fun of them, though in retrospect I could have pointed out that they were butchering the entire English language by speaking in such an affected way. I’m glad I didn’t because it would have been a suicidal act. They may have been from New Jersey, but their mastery of sarcasm and witty banter would have destroyed me within seconds. Not a great start. How did I get so unlucky as to be assigned this roommate? What would we talk about? How would we sleep in the same room? I wanted a brother, this was something entirely different. I finally figured out why we were assigned roommates. It wasn’t scientific. All the freshmen in our unit had last names starting with A and we were both male. We both indicated an interest in Studio Art in our applications, so it was almost a given that we would be selected to room together. The first few weeks were tense, with growing resentment. But there were signs of hope. I became very homesick about a month into the school year. It was a feeling I had never experienced. I lay in my bed, almost unable to move. I noticed that Jonathan was sleeping most of the time as well, and it occurred to me that he might also be feeling homesick. I had invested a lot of energy reducing him to a stereotype. Yet I couldn’t escape the truth: he was just as much a human being as I was. The turning point came one afternoon after classes finished. I returned to the room and decided that instead of reading Art History, I would visit our personal library. We had no television yet. I picked up Ms. Piggy’s Guide to Life , rolled my eyes, and thought, “What the fuck. I’ll read it.” I found the book surprisingly funny and entertaining. I was almost finished when Jonathan walked through the door. I immediately slammed it closed. “Oh sorry, I was bored and borrowed your book.” “And?” That was all he had to say. I responded, “It’s really good. I’m kind of worshiping Ms. Piggy.” His face softened. A smile appeared. I hadn’t seen one since that lunch on orientation day. “I know! She’s like my life.” He was gushing. I looked at him for a moment and then nervously stated, “You know you’re a High-contrast Winter. Do you know what that is?” We’ve been friends ever since.
